items.label: A
items.critique: The bounty frame is plausible, but the reward line is muddled ('I rowed over to have a look when [Person] heard a racket') and the outcome piles up exclamations and stock phrases ('sincere admiration', 'wretched rogue in irons'). It shares a template with B: dead or alive, 'Watch yourself', 'shed a tear', 'in irons', two reward sizes.

items.label: B
items.critique: The pot-seller's grumble has a plain, Nox-like ring, but the lines are built from the same kit as A ('Watch yourself', 'shed a tear', 'in irons', 'Your bounty -- 100 gold!'). The thanks spells out its moral ('Every honest trader on the road can rest easy knowing...'), where Westwood would just say thanks.

items.label: C
items.critique: Casual, offhand voice ('Hi there. Name's...', 'Oh, bah!', 'give ya'). The dry joke about him getting arrested to dodge his responsibilities is pure Nox, and each reward is stated simply alongside a short warning.

items.label: D
items.critique: Short and plain, but 'tithe chest' and 'a mail shirt against the bandits' arrows' are a little ornate for Nox. The two asks don't connect, and the dialect ('doin'', 'do ya?') feels laid on rather than natural.

items.label: E
items.critique: A used-car-salesman gag ('only used it on weekends', 'since I like your face') in short, flat sentences, with a plain price comparison. The pushy sign-off ('I've got someone else interested') is classic Westwood shopkeeper humour.

items.label: F
items.critique: Earnest damsel lines with deadpan humour ('the menfolk... cannot live without us', 'I heard their stomachs grumbling'). The 'Hail, brave Adventurer' register and the follow-up step (the secret passage) match the shape of the campaign's escort quests.

items.label: G
items.critique: The 9,000-gold anvil-and-mule joke aims at Nox's humour, but the outcome lines run long and pile up farewells ('Mind you keep clear... I hope you come through all this in one piece. Farewell!'). The sell-up-before-the-coast framing reads like a generated idea.

items.label: H
items.critique: Breathless, slightly clumsy pleading ('the village north of here and kidnapped almost all of the maidens!', 'Could you... would you get it back for us?') and bare token-of-appreciation thanks, with the run-on comma slips typical of Westwood. Weak but authentic.

tells: Generated texts reuse one stock kit across quests ('Watch yourself', 'shed a tear', 'in irons', 'dead or alive', 'Your bounty -- N gold!'). Westwood's lines vary more and are more specific to the speaker.
Westwood's thanks are bare and brief ('Take these as tokens of my appreciation!'). Generated thanks explain what the deed achieved for the town and pile up exclamations.

Westwood's humour is deadpan and comes from the character (salesman patter, a smuggler who gets arrested on purpose, hungry Ogres). Generated humour is a single set-piece gag, such as an absurd price.

Generated texts use slightly literary or invented nouns ('tithe chest', 'flatboats', 'mail shirt against arrows') and decorative dialect spellings. Westwood keeps its vocabulary plain and modern-casual ('Hi there', 'Oh, bah!', 'check out').

Westwood's two-part quests link their asks into one plot (a jailbreak with two grateful parties, a bow offer and its alternative). Generated pairs are sometimes two unrelated vignettes, or contain muddled connective lines.
